The 7 time-invariant exogenous constructs without indicators can share variance with these baseline-state terms.

reasoning: This is a dynamic structural equation model (DSEM) for daily software debugging performance. The model has three layers: (1) A measurement model linking 26 observed browser-based indicators to 13 latent constructs via factor models with 2 indicators each, where one loading is fixed to 1 for identification. (2) A within-person temporal structural model with AR(1) dynamics for the 9 endogenous time-varying constructs, capturing day-to-day persistence. (3) A time-invariant latent structure where 7 unobserved time-invariant exogenous constructs (developer experience, codebase complexity, etc.) influence endogenous constructs through fixed effects carried across the modeled window. Distribution choices reflect data types: NegativeBinomial for overdispersed browsing counts, Poisson for rare event counts, Bernoulli for binary indicators, OrderedLogistic for ordinal ratings, and Normal for continuous timestamps. Static baseline-state terms on all 13 measured constructs capture persistent baseline differences over the modeled window. The model keeps these baseline-state terms simple to maintain identifiability given the complexity of the structural model (40 causal paths, 9 AR parameters). Code Familiarity is modeled at daily resolution despite weekly granularity, with the expectation that its AR coefficient will be near 1 reflecting slow knowledge accumulation.
